text: The definition takes det G in a chosen integral carrier basis. An integral change of basis has determinant ±1, so its square leaves det G unchanged. Thus this is the signed invariant called discriminant in [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6), with the site’s explicit determinant naming. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Gram.lean#L225) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L249) passes.
The chosen-basis value equals the Gram determinant in every integral basis.
The hyperbolic determinant is −1, retaining its sign.

The basis correspondence is an integral linear equivalence, and equal Gram entries imply preservation of all pairings by bilinearity. Extending this equivalence rationally gives the carrier-preserving isometry described in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). The Gram equality is an explicit hypothesis. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Gram.lean#L359) passes.
The constructed ambient isometry takes each embedded source basis vector to the corresponding target basis vector.

The matrix has integer entry B(ei,ej), using the restricted integral form and the supplied carrier basis. This is exactly the Gram convention in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). Entrywise construction needs no separately supplied Fintype instance. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Gram.lean#L83) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L103) passes.
Each matrix entry is the integral pairing of its indexed basis vectors.
The standard hyperbolic basis produces [[0,1],[1,0]].

The chosen-basis determinant equals that in e because the change matrix is integral unimodular and acts by PᵀGP. Its determinant contributes det(P)²=1, giving exactly the basis-independent signed value of [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Gram.lean#L180) passes.
Equality holds even when the two integral bases use different finite index types.

In an extended rational carrier basis, the determinant is the integer Gram determinant cast to ℚ. The injective cast preserves nonvanishing, and [Mathlib’s determinant criterion](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/BilinearForm.lean#L499) identifies this with nondegeneracy. The zero-dimensional case correctly has determinant 1. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L261) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L249) passes.
The degenerate affine form has determinant zero.
The indefinite hyperbolic form has nonzero determinant −1.

This is Matrix.det of the integral Gram matrix, so it is the signed quantity in [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). Finite indexing and decidable equality support the determinant construction; the definition does not require nondegeneracy. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Gram.lean#L152) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Gram.lean#L209) passes.
The value unfolds to the ordinary matrix determinant.
For a prescribed Gram matrix the value is exactly det G.

The equality unfolds gramDet as det(gramMatrix e), with no absolute value or sign correction. This is the signed Gram determinant used in [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Gram.lean#L209) passes.
The constructor specialization returns det G exactly.

Both matrix constructions evaluate at (i,j) as the integral pairing B(ei,ej). Once finite indexing is supplied, the auxiliary entrywise matrix therefore equals [Mathlib’s matrix of a bilinear form](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/BilinearForm.lean#L196), with the same basis in both arguments. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Gram.lean#L83) passes.
Entry evaluation identifies both sides with the same integral bilinear value.

The canonical carrier basis has Gram matrix G, and the lattice determinant equals the Gram determinant in any carrier basis. Combining these facts yields det G exactly, as in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3) and [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6), including singular G. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L249) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L261) passes.
The indefinite matrix gives signed determinant −1.
The singular affine matrix gives determinant zero.

Reindexing aligns the finite basis index sets; simultaneous row and column permutation preserves determinant. An integral basis change then gives PᵀGP with det(P)=±1, so the signed determinants agree. This justifies the basis-free invariant in [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Gram.lean#L174) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Gram.lean#L225) passes.
Reindexing both arguments of the Gram matrix leaves its determinant unchanged.
The chosen-basis invariant agrees with every carrier basis.

The matrix in the extended rational basis is the entrywise cast of the integer Gram matrix. Applying [Mathlib’s determinant criterion](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/BilinearForm.lean#L499) and injectivity of ℤ→ℚ gives exactly the displayed nonvanishing equivalence. No positivity assumption is introduced. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Gram.lean#L239) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L261) passes.
The same criterion passes to the basis-independent determinant.
The singular affine example has zero determinant.

The entrywise definition evaluates the restricted integral form at ei,ej, precisely the Gram entry in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). It preserves the supplied order of the two indices and performs no scalar extension. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L301) passes.
Evaluating a prescribed Gram construction recovers the integer entry Gij.

For each i,j, the embedded carrier basis vectors have integral pairing Gij. Matrix extensionality therefore recovers the entire supplied G, exactly the Gram reconstruction convention in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). Singular matrices are included. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L103) passes.
The hyperbolic constructor recovers its complete integer matrix, including off-diagonal ones.

The value is natAbs of the signed determinant, the nonnegative quantity in [Dolgachev §1.2’s absolute Gram determinant](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4). It differs deliberately from the signed quantity called discriminant in [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). The hyperbolic example distinguishes the two conventions. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L255) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L108) passes.
The hyperbolic lattice has discriminant 1 despite signed determinant −1.
The rank-one parameter a gives nonnegative discriminant |a|.

The canonical integral basis has matrix G, so taking its matrix determinant gives exactly G.det. This is the signed Gram convention in [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6); neither nonsingularity nor a positive-definite hypothesis is needed. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Gram.lean#L232) passes.
The basis-independent signed determinant has the same value det G.

Determinant commutes with the ring map ℤ→ℚ, and the cast Gram matrix is the ambient form matrix in the extended basis. Thus the displayed rational determinant is the cast of the integer one, using [Mathlib’s matrix of a bilinear form](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/BilinearForm.lean#L196) and the polynomial determinant formula. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Gram.lean#L133) passes.
The underlying matrices already agree entrywise under scalar extension.

The constructed lattice has determinant det G; its assumed nonvanishing therefore gives nondegeneracy by [Mathlib’s determinant criterion](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/BilinearForm.lean#L499). The conclusion is the separate IsNondegenerate mixin, with no assertion of definiteness or unimodularity. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Gram.lean#L232) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L336) passes.
The constructed determinant is the supplied matrix determinant.
The singular affine constructor shows why the nonzero-determinant premise matters.

The integral and rational forms have the same Gram matrix up to the injective integer cast. Applying [Mathlib’s determinant criterion](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/BilinearForm.lean#L499) over ℤ and ℚ gives equivalent nonzero-determinant conditions. This concerns zero radical, not perfection of the integral pairing. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L102) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L137) passes.
The rank-one determinant is a, so nonzero parameters such as 2 need not be units.
Perfect/unimodular rank-one pairing requires the stronger unit condition.

The equality unfolds discriminant as determinant.natAbs, fixing the docstring’s nonnegative convention, corresponding to [Dolgachev §1.2’s absolute Gram determinant](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4). It keeps the signed determinant as a separate invariant. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L255) passes.
The negative hyperbolic determinant produces positive discriminant 1.

Basis independence identifies the signed determinant with gramDet e; applying natAbs yields the stated formula in any integral basis. For nondegenerate lattices this is the quantity in [Dolgachev §1.2’s absolute Gram determinant](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4); the definition also permits zero for degenerate forms. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L108) passes.
The formula gives |a| for every rank-one parameter, including zero.

Each cast entry is the ambient pairing of the embedded integral basis vectors, and the extended rational basis consists of those same vectors. Hence the matrices agree entrywise, precisely the scalar-extension interpretation of [Mathlib’s matrix of a bilinear form](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/BilinearForm.lean#L196). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Gram.lean#L122) passes.
The scalar-extension equality holds for each indexed entry.

The Gram entry is the restricted integer pairing; its cast equals the ambient rational pairing by integralForm_cast. Thus both sides evaluate the same basis vectors, consistently with the Gram definition in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean#L301) passes.
A prescribed Gram construction recovers Gij before casting.

For each A this is the ordinary convolution group quotient by the points vanishing on I; hI supplies the normality required by [Milne, §5.a](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=109). Published [kernel](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Presheaf.lean#L83) and [surjectivity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Presheaf.lean#L109) controls pass. It constructs a group at each value algebra, without claiming representability or sheaf descent.
The quotient projection kernel is exactly the cut-out subgroup.
Every abstract quotient class has an ambient representative.

The morphism sends an ambient point to its coset modulo V(I)(A), the canonical projection of [Milne, §5.a](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=109). Published [class-evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Presheaf.lean#L72) and [kernel](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Presheaf.lean#L83) controls pass. Its source is G(A), and its target is the abstract quotient group, not the points of a separately constructed quotient scheme.
The bundled projection is the ordinary coset map.
The quotient projection kernel is exactly the cut-out subgroup.

Unfolding the bundled projection gives the ordinary coset map of [Milne, §5.a](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=109). The published [identity-class control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Presheaf.lean#L95) passes, identifying exactly which representatives become trivial. The local Normal instance comes from the supplied hI; its proof does not change the quotient relation or the represented class.
The class is identity exactly when its representative lies in the denominator.

Every element of the abstract quotient has an ambient representative, giving the surjection in [Milne, §5.a](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=109). The published [factorization-uniqueness control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Presheaf.lean#L248) passes and uses determination by those representatives. This is surjectivity onto G(A)/V(I)(A); it makes no assertion that points of a geometric quotient lift over A.
A homomorphism from the quotient is determined by its composite with the projection.

Postcomposition by χ preserves vanishing on I, so it induces a homomorphism of quotient groups by [Mathlib’s induced quotient map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/GroupTheory/QuotientGroup/Defs.lean#L280). Published [representative-evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Presheaf.lean#L130) and [subgroup-preservation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Naturality.lean#L77) controls pass. The direction is covariant in value algebras A→B; neither injectivity nor surjectivity of χ is required.
Changing value algebra sends the class of g to the class of its postcomposition.
Postcomposition preserves vanishing on I.

The induced map sends [g] to [χ∘g], exactly the class formula in [Mathlib’s induced quotient map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/GroupTheory/QuotientGroup/Defs.lean#L280). The published [kernel-comparison naturality control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Presheaf.lean#L82) passes as a concrete specialization. The formula holds for every representative because postcomposition carries the normal denominator into the target denominator.
The kernel comparison commutes with every value-algebra morphism.

The assignment A↦G(A)/V(I)(A), with postcomposition on classes, is the functor D used in [Milne, Theorem 5.13](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=112). Published [object](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Presheaf.lean#L173) and [morphism](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Presheaf.lean#L181) controls pass. Identity and composition follow from quotient-map functoriality; the declaration is a group-valued presheaf and imposes no sheaf condition.
The functor value is the specified abstract quotient group.
The functor map is the induced quotient map with object transports.

At A the functor evaluates to precisely G(A)/V(I)(A), the pointwise construction in [Milne, Theorem 5.13](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=112). The published [projection-kernel control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Presheaf.lean#L83) passes and confirms the denominator. This is equality of bundled groups at the same A, with no sheafification or replacement of the quotient by points of a scheme.
The quotient projection kernel is exactly the cut-out subgroup.

The functor acts on quotient groups by [Mathlib’s induced quotient map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/GroupTheory/QuotientGroup/Defs.lean#L280). The published [class-evaluation control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Presheaf.lean#L130) passes, identifying its value as [g]↦[χ∘g]. The eqToHom factors only transport the displayed object equalities; their directions correctly start at the A-object and finish at the B-object.
Changing value algebra sends the class of g to the class of its postcomposition.

The component g↦[g] commutes with value-algebra postcomposition, giving the natural projection to the functor in [Milne, Theorem 5.13](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=112). Published [component](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Presheaf.lean#L213) and [naturality-on-classes](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Presheaf.lean#L130) controls pass. Its codomain is the pointwise quotient presheaf; the declaration does not identify this presheaf with an fppf quotient sheaf.
Each natural projection component is the ordinary quotient projection.
Changing value algebra sends the class of g to the class of its postcomposition.

At A the natural projection is the ordinary quotient homomorphism followed by the object-identification transport, matching [Milne, §5.a](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=109). The published [identity-class control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Presheaf.lean#L95) passes. The transport points toward the functor object and leaves the coset unchanged, so its kernel remains the subgroup vanishing on I.
The class is identity exactly when its representative lies in the denominator.

A group homomorphism killing V(I)(A) descends by [g]↦f(g), the universal property implemented by [Mathlib’s quotient-group lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/GroupTheory/QuotientGroup/Defs.lean#L226). Published [factorization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Presheaf.lean#L233) and [uniqueness](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Presheaf.lean#L248) controls pass. The hypothesis is subgroup containment in f’s kernel; the target is any group of the stated universe, without representability assumptions.

The kernel comparison sends a source-point class to its image under f.

Comparison surjectivity is equivalent to original point-map surjectivity.
The comparison is an isomorphism exactly under point-map surjectivity.

Membership means that at least one coordinate equals 0 or 1, exactly the boundary used in the finite cubical definition. For an empty index type the existential is false, giving the required empty boundary of the one-point zero cube. For arbitrary infinite N this is explicitly a coordinate-face subset, not an assertion about the ambient topological frontier. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, cubical boundary and zero-dimensional convention](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L60).

LoopSpace X x is exactly the type of continuous paths on the unit interval with both endpoints x. Its inherited topology is induced by the compact-open topology on C(I,X). It contains parameterized loops themselves, before quotienting by endpoint-fixing homotopy. Compared with [Chapter 1 §2, p.6, loops and endpoint-fixing homotopy](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf); [Proposition A.14 and discussion, pp.530–531, based loop subspace of the mapping space](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L87).

The subset consists of continuous cube maps taking every coordinate face to the specified basepoint. With N=Fin n it is the usual cubical loop model; the boundary condition applies at every face, not just at the vertices. When N is empty it imposes no condition, so the resulting space is homeomorphic to X. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, maps (Iⁿ,∂Iⁿ)→(X,x)](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L98).

This is the constant continuous cube map with value x, and therefore satisfies every boundary condition for any index type. It supplies the distinguished generalized loop. In positive dimension its class is the group identity; in zero dimension it represents the point x among all points of X. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, constant-map identity and zero-dimensional model](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L146).

The relation is homotopy relative to the entire cubical boundary. Since both endpoint maps equal x there, every intermediate map also sends that boundary to x. This is precisely the equivalence relation used for based cubical homotopy classes, rather than unrestricted homotopy of the underlying maps. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, homotopies preserve the boundary basepoint at all times](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L234).

The quotient identifies generalized loops exactly by homotopy relative to the boundary. On Fin n this matches the classical cubical πₙ. The underlying definition is a type of classes for every index type; the separate algebraic instances correctly require nonempty indices for a group and two distinct indices for commutativity. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, quotient definition and low-dimensional cases](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf); [Chapter 9 §1, p.65, group and abelian-group thresholds](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L441).

The abbreviation uses Fin n, hence exactly n unit-interval coordinates, with no dimension shift. It specializes the arbitrary-index quotient to the standard πₙ(X,x). The zero- and one-dimensional comparison declarations confirm the intended indexing. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, n-cube definition](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf); [Chapter 9 §1, p.65, π₀ and π₁ compatibility](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L460).

Along coordinate i the first half traverses f at doubled speed and the second half traverses g. At the seam both values are x by the boundary condition; the other coordinates remain unchanged. The interval projections merely supply bounded coordinates and do not alter the classical branch formulas on their respective halves. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, cubical concatenation formula](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L402).

The chosen coordinate is replaced by 1−tᵢ, and every other coordinate is retained. This reverses the associated curried loop and preserves all boundary faces, giving the correct representative of inversion. It is a concrete operation on generalized loops before taking classes. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, cubical inverse formula](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L417).

Choosing a coordinate identifies these classes with the fundamental group of the complementary generalized-loop space, transporting its group structure. Nonempty N is exactly what permits this choice. The existing coordinate-independence theorem shows the resulting law is independent of which coordinate was chosen. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, group structure from one-coordinate composition](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf); [Chapter 9 §1, p.65, iterated-loop description](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L550).

Nontrivial N supplies two distinct directions. Their concatenations have a common constant-loop unit and satisfy interchange, so the Eckmann–Hilton argument makes the existing group multiplication commutative. This matches the classical n≥2 threshold and remains valid for arbitrary index types with two distinct elements. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, commutativity uses two coordinates and leaves the others fixed](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf); [Chapter 9 §1, p.65, abelian groups for n≥2](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L606).

The product [p][q] is represented by q followed by p along coordinate i. This reversal matches the inherited fundamental-group End multiplication and May’s composition convention. The source’s coordinate-independence result makes the formula valid for any supplied i, not just the coordinate chosen by the group instance. Compared with [Chapter 1 §2, p.6, [g][f] traverses f then g](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf); [§4.1 p.340, underlying coordinate concatenation](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L590).

Inversion of the class of p is represented by reversing coordinate i. The inverse law is transported from reversal in the associated fundamental group, and the source proves that reversing any other coordinate yields the same class. This is a statement on classes, not equality of the different raw reversals. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, inverse by coordinate reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf); [Chapter 1 §2, pp.6–7, loop inverse](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L598).

The multiplicative identity is the class of the constant cube map at x. Under the curried-loop equivalence this is the constant loop at the constant complementary cube, hence the fundamental-group identity. The Nonempty N hypothesis retains the positive-dimensional group scope. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, identity is the constant basepoint map](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L586).

With no coordinates the cube has one point and its boundary is empty. Evaluation at that unique cube point and the constant-map construction are inverse continuous maps, yielding the stated homeomorphism with X. The inverse may use any y∈X, so it does not restrict to the component of the parameter x. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, zero cube is a point with empty boundary; Proposition A.14(a), p.530, evaluation continuity](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L466).

For Fin 0 the cube is a point and a relative homotopy is just a path between its two values. Quotienting therefore gives all path components of X. The result is a set equivalence, correctly avoiding a general group structure or restriction to the basepoint’s component. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, π₀ is the set of path components](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L491).

A singleton index type identifies each cube point with its sole interval coordinate. The forward map evaluates p on the constant-coordinate tuple; the inverse evaluates a path at the unique coordinate. The face condition becomes exactly the two endpoint conditions p(0)=p(1)=x. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, one-cube based maps](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf); [Chapter 1 §2, p.6, based loops](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L495).

With one coordinate, the cube boundary is its two endpoints, so relative homotopy of generalized loops is exactly endpoint-fixing loop homotopy. The source converts representatives and homotopies in both directions, producing the asserted equivalence with the fundamental group. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, n=1 model](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf); [Chapter 1 §2, pp.6–7, fundamental group as loop classes](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L533).

Uncurrying sends p to the map y↦p(y|M)(y|N); the inverse curries in those same coordinates. A face in M makes the outer loop the constant inner loop, while a face in N makes the inner value x. The compact-open exponential law yields a homeomorphism: both arbitrary products of unit intervals are compact Hausdorff, so its domain hypotheses are met. Compared with [Propositions A.14 and A.16, pp.530–532, continuity and homeomorphism of currying](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L220).

The selected coordinate i becomes the path parameter and the remaining coordinates index each generalized-loop value. At parameter 0 or 1, the original map lies on a face and is identically x, giving the constant complementary loop as both endpoints. Currying is continuous for the compact-open topology because the complementary cube is compact Hausdorff. Compared with [Proposition A.14, pp.530–531, currying continuity](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf); [Chapter 9 §1, p.65, passage to iterated loop spaces](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L267).

Natural primality is defined by irreducibility, and prime_def proves the usual criterion: p≥2 and every natural divisor is 1 or p. Thus 0 and 1 are excluded and 2 is included. The irreducibility formulation has the intended meaning for the prime parameter of ℤₚ. Compared with [the reference](https://www.cs.toronto.edu/~david/course-notes/csc110-111/07-number-theory/01-number-theory-definitions.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Nat/Prime/Defs.lean#L42).

The closed unit ball in ℚₚ is a commutative subring: the ultrametric inequality gives additive closure, norm multiplicativity gives multiplicative closure, and negation preserves the norm. The derived CommRing uses these inherited operations. Its prime hypothesis excludes composite and degenerate parameters. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/math5020f11/breuningnotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/PadicIntegers.lean#L72).

The chosen topology on ℕ is discrete: every subset is open. Mathlib writes this topology as ⊥ because its order on topologies reverses inclusion of open sets. This is the usual discrete index space for sequences and finitely supported functions. Compared with [the reference](https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/morris.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Order.lean#L578).

The DiscreteTopology instance certifies that the chosen topology on ℕ is the all-subsets topology. Its proof is definitional because the TopologicalSpace instance is already ⊥. It does not change the topology or impose a convergence condition on sequences. Compared with [the reference](https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/morris.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Order.lean#L579).

Every function from a discrete space to any topological space is continuous, since each preimage of an open set is open. Discreteness is required of the domain; no separation, finiteness or discreteness assumption on the codomain is needed. Compared with [the reference](https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/morris.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Order.lean#L334).

DiscreteTopology states that the supplied topology has every subset open, encoded as equality with ⊥. The reverse order convention for Mathlib topologies accounts for this symbol. It imposes no cardinality restriction and also covers the empty space. Compared with [the reference](https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/morris.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Order.lean#L309).

OpenAddSubgroup bundles an additive subgroup whose carrier is open in the given topology. The definition itself needs no continuity of the ambient group operations. Under the usual topological-group hypotheses it is precisely an open subgroup in the classical sense. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/OpenSubgroup.lean#L44).

IsTopologicalRing requires joint continuity of addition and multiplication and continuity of negation. It agrees with the standard notion on ordinary rings, while allowing nonunital, nonassociative and non-Hausdorff rings. Explicit negation continuity is appropriate in that broader setting. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/math5020f11/breuningnotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Ring/Basic.lean#L60).

IsTopologicalAddGroup combines joint continuity of addition with continuity of negation. This is the standard topological-group definition in additive notation. Neither commutativity nor a Hausdorff assumption is hidden in the class. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Group/Defs.lean#L100).

ContinuousMul states joint continuity of the binary multiplication map from M×M to M. It supplies the topological compatibility condition alone; associativity and an identity must come from separate algebraic hypotheses. It is stronger than continuity with either input fixed. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Monoid/Defs.lean#L53).

ContinuousAdd requires joint continuity of (x,y)↦x+y. It makes no algebraic assertion about associativity, commutativity or zero. Combined with the corresponding algebraic structure, it expresses the usual topological compatibility for addition. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Monoid/Defs.lean#L42).

The docstring calls multiplication “addition”, but the class requires only Mul and its two fields express continuity of left and right multiplication; there is no Add requirement. The intended mathematical class is correct: the docstring should say “multiplication”, consistent with the standard separate-continuity convention in [Banakh–Bardyla–Ravsky, Introduction](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1902.08760). See the [pinned definition](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Monoid/Defs.lean#L62).

IsSemitopologicalRing keeps addition jointly continuous and negation continuous, while requiring only separate continuity of multiplication. The fields implement exactly this stated weakening of a topological ring; they do not infer joint multiplication continuity. Compared with [the reference](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1902.08760) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Ring/Basic.lean#L82).

IsSemitopologicalSemiring requires joint continuity of addition and separate continuity of multiplication. The asymmetric continuity requirements are explicit in both fields and documentation. It allows nonunital and nonassociative semirings without asserting that multiplication is jointly continuous. Compared with [the reference](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1902.08760) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Ring/Basic.lean#L72).

IsTopologicalSemiring requires both addition and multiplication to be jointly continuous. This matches the standard topological-semiring definition, extended explicitly to nonunital and nonassociative semirings. No Hausdorff or cancellation hypothesis is needed for the compatibility property. Compared with [the reference](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40687-024-00467-6) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Ring/Basic.lean#L52).

SMulCommClass expresses commuting scalar operations: m•(n•a)=n•(m•a). It is the compatibility needed to scale linear maps over another scalar ring. The two scalar types may differ; no action of one scalar type on the other is assumed. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/dualmod.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Action/Defs.lean#L146).

RingHomInvPair contains both inverse laws: σ′∘σ=id and σ∘σ′=id. It therefore expresses a genuine inverse pair of semiring homomorphisms, suitable for reversing semilinear equivalences. The second field’s prose repeats σ′ by typo; its displayed equation has the correct order. Compared with [the reference](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/CompTypeclasses.lean#L83).

RingHomCompTriple records σ₂₃∘σ₁₂=σ₁₃ with the correct source and target rings. It is the compatibility required when composing semilinear maps. The order is first σ₁₂, then σ₂₃; no injectivity, surjectivity or inverse is asserted. Compared with [the reference](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/CompTypeclasses.lean#L64).

Multiplicative Archimedeanness passes from an ordered commutative monoid to its units: apply the original power bound to their underlying values. The order and powers on units are inherited, so the same natural exponent works. No ring, norm or completeness assumption is used. Compared with [the reference](https://people.math.wisc.edu/~angenent/521.2017s/SequencesinR.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Basic.lean#L490).

Nonnegative reals are multiplicatively Archimedean: for y>1, its natural powers eventually exceed any prescribed nonnegative x. The inherited instance uses the ordinary Archimedean property and a Bernoulli bound. Zero targets are allowed; bases zero and one are correctly excluded by y>1. Compared with [the reference](https://people.math.wisc.edu/~angenent/521.2017s/SequencesinR.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L87).
